newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger expects to be PM for three year term.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger expects to be PM for three year term.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Wednesday he expects to remain in the role of prime minister throughout the new three-year parliamentary term.
Bolger was speaking shortly after his caretaker conservative National Party signed a coalition deal with the nationalist New Zealand First Party.
The deal, announced on Tuesday night, ended nearly two months of political suspense over who power-broker NZ First would choose as its coalition partner.
Bolger has been prime minister since 1990 and political analysts expect this term to be his last.
Bolger's number two in the new government is NZ First leader Winston Peters, who along with the role of Deputy Prime Minister has snapped up a newly created position of Treasurer.
Peters formed the NZ First Party in 1993, after Bolger sacked him as a National Party minister in 1991.
